children: Amazon announced the launch of TorchNeuron on October 19 local time, an open-source tool designed to make it easier for developers to move from Nvidia chips to Amazon’s in-house AI chips. According to ChainCatcher, the tool lets AI code written in PyTorch run on Amazon chips without being rewritten, challenging the software advantage Nvidia has built around CUDA.

Annapurna Labs, Amazon’s chip-design division, said developers can run the same code on its Trainium chips by changing just one configuration setting. PyTorch, maintained primarily by Meta, is described as an open-source framework used by most AI developers. Amazon planned to make TorchNeuron freely available as open-source software on October 20 at the PyTorch conference in San Jose, California.

Annapurna Labs software vice president Colin Brace said the tool is intended to reduce the steps needed to try Amazon’s chips and accommodate customers’ existing workflows. He said more than 30 early customers across areas including robotics, world models, and voice AI are already using it, and that switching to Amazon chips can reduce costs.

title: Amazon Launches Open-Source TorchNeuron Tool to Ease Shift to Its AI Chips
